newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse ends firm, seen testing 1,200pts.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse ends firm, seen testing 1,200pts.

text.p: Greek stocks ended up 1.49 percent on Wednesday with market watchers saying sentiment continued to be bullish. The next test would be at the resistance level of 1,200 points.

"The market continued strong on Wednesday. Now, the new resistance level is set at 1,200 points," said Konstantinos Xenos, an analyst at Telesis Securities. There was a clear rotation from banking shares to other sectors, he said.
"This is an across-the-board spread from banks to industrial and construction stocks, which have more upside potential. This is no longer a banking shares' monopoly," he added.
Shares of OTE have started a second round, Xenos said. On Wednesday, they closed 85 drachmas up at 5,450.
The Athens general share index closed 1.49 percent or 17.30 points higher at 1179.84 from Tuesday's 1162.54, after opening at 1160.26.
Wednesday's turnover was strong at 14.4 billion drachmas on volume of 5.2 million shares, with block trades in OTE, Titan, Alte, Alpha Credit, Shelman and National Mortgage Bank.
Gainers led losers 128 to 86 with 36 issues unchanged on 250 traded.
Insurance shares led the way with a rise of 2.11 percent and banks closely following with 2.09 percent. Construction and leasing shares slipped 0.08 percent.
Industrials gained 1.27 percent and investment shares rose 0.77 percent. Small caps ended 0.21 percent up.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 914.00-932.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, climbed 85 drachmas to close at 5,450.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $23.11-$24.11. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 8,494-9,023 drachmas.
